result:
Solution 3 has the correct answer. The vanishing set is the set of primes where the modular curve $X_0(p)$ has genus $0$, which is $\{2,3,5,7,13\}$, so the sum is $30$.

Solution 1 gets the set wrong: it omits $p=13$. $X_0(13)$ has genus $0$, so $H^3$ vanishes there too. Its claim that the genus vanishes only for $p=2,3,5,7$ is false. Solution 2's set $\{2,3,5\}$ is also wrong, since $p=7$ also gives vanishing.

Solution 3's reduction to the boundary system is the right idea, and its finite checks at $p=7$, $11$, $13$ are consistent with the genus picture. I have not re-derived the full computation, so this rests on that structure and on my recollection of the Miller–Patzt–Putman result for $\Gamma_{0,3}^+(p)$.

CHOICE: 3
